title: Multiplying two brackets
objectives: Expand $(x + a)(x + b)$ with an area model
Say which piece of the rectangle each term comes from

screens.prose: A rectangle is $x + 3$ wide and $x + 2$ tall. Two cuts split it into four pieces.
screens.question: Take $x = 10$. What is the area of the whole rectangle?

hints.text: How wide and how tall is the rectangle when $x = 10$?
The width is $10 + 3$ and the height is $10 + 2$.
The rectangle is 13 wide and 12 tall, so its area is $13 \times 12$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the full width and the full height first, then multiply.

byKey.firsts-lasts: You multiplied $10 \times 10$ and $3 \times 2$, then added. That leaves out the two strips along the edges.
byKey.added: You added the width and the height. Area is width times height.
byKey.one-strip: You missed the bottom strip. It is 2 tall and 10 wide, so it adds 20.
byKey.other-strip: You missed the right-hand strip. It is 10 tall and 3 wide, so it adds 30.

explain.text: The rectangle is $13 \times 12 = 156$. Piece by piece it is $100 + 30 + 20 + 6 = 156$. Every piece counts, the two strips included.

screens.prose: Now let $x$ change. Picture the rectangle growing as $x$ grows, while the 3 and the 2 stay fixed.
screens.question: Tap every piece whose area changes when $x$ changes.

hints.text: Which pieces have $x$ along one of their sides?
The bottom right piece is 2 tall and 3 wide.
Three pieces touch an $x$ edge: the square and the two strips.

feedback.correct: Three pieces grow with $x$. The corner stays at 6.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Pick the pieces with $x$ along one side.

byKey.c22: That corner is 2 by 3 whatever $x$ is. Its area is always 6.
byKey.square-only: The square grows, but so do the two strips. Each has $x$ along one side.
byKey.strips-only: The strips grow, and so does the square: it is $x$ by $x$.
byKey.all: The corner is 2 by 3 for every $x$, so its area never changes.

explain.text: The square is $x$ by $x$, area $x^2$. The strips are $3x$ and $2x$, and the corner is always $2 \times 3 = 6$. So the area is $x^2 + 3x + 2x + 6$.

screens.prose: We write the area as $(x + 4)(x + 5)$. Rewriting it as a sum of separate terms is called **expanding** the brackets.
screens.question: Place the area of each piece of $(x + 4)(x + 5)$. Leave the spare tokens.

hints.text: Each piece is its height times its width.
The corner piece is 4 tall and 5 wide.
Square $x^2$, strips $5x$ and $4x$, corner $4 \times 5 = 20$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply each piece's height by its width.

byKey.t9: You added 4 and 5. The corner is 4 by 5, so its area is 20.
byKey.t2x: You added $x$ and $x$. The square is $x$ by $x$, so its area is $x^2$.
byKey.tsq: $x^2$ is the square, $x$ by $x$, at the top left.
byKey.t5x: $5x$ is the piece $x$ tall and 5 wide, at the top right.
byKey.t4x: $4x$ is the piece 4 tall and $x$ wide, at the bottom left.
byKey.t20: 20 is the corner, 4 by 5, at the bottom right.

explain.text: The pieces are $x^2$, $5x$, $4x$ and 20, so $(x + 4)(x + 5) = x^2 + 5x + 4x + 20$. The two strips are both $x$ terms. Collected, they make $9x$.

screens.prose: A new rectangle: $x + 2$ wide and $x + 6$ tall. Expand, then collect the two strips into one term.
screens.question: Which is $(x + 6)(x + 2)$ expanded and simplified?

options.why: You multiplied the firsts and the lasts and skipped the two strips.
You multiplied 6 and 2 for the strips and added them for the corner. The strips add; the corner multiplies.
You added 6 and 2 for the corner. It is 6 by 2, so its area is 12.

hints.text: Find the two strips and the corner.
The strips are $2x$ and $6x$.
Strips: $2x + 6x = 8x$. Corner: $6 \times 2 = 12$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find each of the four pieces, then collect the strips.

explain.text: The strips give $2x + 6x = 8x$ and the corner gives 12. So $(x + 6)(x + 2) = x^2 + 8x + 12$. The two numbers add to make the middle term and multiply to make the last.

screens.prose: A bracket can hold a minus, and a negative length makes no rectangle. A grid does the same job: each cell is its row times its column.

state.caption: Each cell is its row times its column

screens.question: $(x + 5)(x - 2) = x^2 + bx - 10$. What is $b$?

hints.text: Which two cells hold $x$ terms?
The $x$ cells are $x \times 5$ and $-2 \times x$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Fill in the two $x$ cells, signs included, then add them.

byKey.ignored-sign: You added $5x$ and $2x$. The 2 is subtracted, so that cell is $-2x$.
byKey.flipped: You made $5x$ the negative one. The minus belongs to the 2, so it is $5x - 2x$.
byKey.both-minus: Only the 2 carries a minus. The $5x$ cell stays positive.

explain.text: The $x$ cells are $5x$ and $-2x$, which collect to $3x$. So $(x + 5)(x - 2) = x^2 + 3x - 10$. The corner, $5 \times (-2) = -10$, is negative too.

state.caption: Each cell is its row times its column

options.why: You kept a minus on the corner. Minus 3 times minus 5 is plus 15.
You dropped the minus signs on the strips. Each is $x$ times a negative number.
You multiplied the firsts and the lasts and skipped the two $x$ cells.

hints.text: Fill the three empty cells, signs included.
The corner is $(-3) \times (-5)$.
Cells: $-5x$, $-3x$ and $+15$. Collect the $x$ cells.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out each cell with its sign, then collect.

explain.text: The $x$ cells are $-5x$ and $-3x$, which collect to $-8x$. The corner is $(-3) \times (-5) = +15$. So $(x - 3)(x - 5) = x^2 - 8x + 15$.

screens.prose: Sam squares a bracket and writes $(x + 3)^2 = x^2 + 9$. Here is the square with side $x + 3$.
screens.question: Is Sam right?

options.why: You squared each term on its own. That keeps the square and the corner but drops the two $3x$ strips.
You counted one strip. There is a $3x$ strip along the top and another down the side.
You doubled 3 for the corner. The corner is 3 by 3, so its area is 9.

hints.text: Test both sides with $x = 1$.
Look at the two pieces along the edges.
$(1 + 3)^2 = 16$ but $1 + 9 = 10$. The missing 6 is the two strips.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all four pieces of the square.

byKey.sam: You agreed with Sam, who squared each term. At $x = 1$ the square is $4^2 = 16$, but $x^2 + 9$ gives 10.

explain.text: Sam kept the $x^2$ square and the 9 corner but lost the two $3x$ strips. So $(x + 3)^2 = x^2 + 6x + 9$. A squared bracket always has a middle term: twice the number, times $x$.

screens.prose: Every time, you found four pieces: a square, two strips and a corner. Now take any numbers $a$ and $b$.
screens.question: Put the lines in order to expand $(x + a)(x + b)$.

lines.text: $(x + a)(x + b) = x(x + b) + a(x + b)$, split the rectangle into its two rows
$= x^2 + bx + ax + ab$, multiply out each row
$= x^2 + (a + b)x + ab$, collect the two strips

hints.text: Which line still has both brackets in it?
The middle line has four separate terms: the four pieces.
Split into rows, multiply out each row, then collect.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start with the line that still has brackets, and end with the collected form.

explain.text: You split the rectangle into two rows, then each row into two pieces. The strips $bx$ and $ax$ collect into $(a + b)x$. So the middle number is the sum $a + b$ and the last is the product $ab$.

screens.prose: You invest £2,000 for two years at a rate $r$ a year, with interest added each year. It grows to $2000(1 + r)^2$.

state.caption: Each pound grows to $(1 + r)^2$ in two years

screens.question: Take $r = 0.04$. How much of the final value is interest on interest, the $r^2$ piece?

hints.text: Which piece of the square is $r^2$?
The small corner is $r$ by $r$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the $r^2$ corner for one pound, then scale it to £2,000.

byKey.whole-gain: That is the whole gain. Only the small corner is interest earned on interest.
byKey.one-strip: That is one strip: a year of plain interest on £2,000. The $r^2$ piece is the small corner.
byKey.two-strips: That is both strips: two years of plain interest. The $r^2$ piece is the small corner.
byKey.per-pound: That is $r^2$ for each pound. Multiply by the £2,000 invested.

explain.text: Each strip is $2000 \times 0.04 = \text{£}80$ of plain interest. The corner is $2000 \times 0.0016 = \text{£}3.20$, interest earned on the first year's interest. In all, $2000 + 80 + 80 + 3.20 = \text{£}2163.20$.

ideas: Multiplying two brackets makes four pieces: every term of one bracket meets every term of the other.
For $(x + a)(x + b)$ the two strips collect to $(a + b)x$ and the corner is $ab$.
A squared bracket is a square with two equal strips: $(x + a)^2 = x^2 + 2ax + a^2$.

formula.name: Expanding two brackets
formula.note: Add the numbers for the middle term; multiply them for the last.

summary.trap: $(x + 3)^2$ is not $x^2 + 9$. The two $3x$ strips make it $x^2 + 6x + 9$.

options.why: You multiplied the firsts and the lasts. The two strips, $3x$ and $7x$, are missing.
You multiplied for the middle and added for the end. The strips add; the corner multiplies.
You added 7 and 3 for the last term. The corner is $7 \times 3 = 21$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find all four pieces, then collect.

explain.text: The four pieces are $x^2$, $3x$, $7x$ and 21. The strips collect to $10x$. So $(x + 7)(x + 3) = x^2 + 10x + 21$.

options.why: You made both strips negative. They are $-4x$ and $+4x$, which cancel.
You made the corner positive. It is $4 \times (-4) = -16$.
You doubled 4 for the corner. It is $4 \times (-4) = -16$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write out all four pieces with their signs.

explain.text: The pieces are $x^2$, $-4x$, $+4x$ and $-16$. The two strips cancel, so there is no middle term. This edge case comes back in lesson 4.

quiz.prose: A return $r$ has a mean of $m$. A measure of spread uses the squared deviation $(r - m)^2$.
quiz.question: Which is $(r - m)^2$ expanded?

options.why: You squared $r$ and $m$ and kept the minus between them. The two $-mr$ strips are missing, and the corner is $(-m)^2 = +m^2$.
You squared each term and dropped the middle. Two strips of $-mr$ belong there.
The corner is $(-m) \times (-m)$, which is $+m^2$.

feedback.correct: Square, two strips of $-mr$, and a positive corner.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write $(r - m)(r - m)$ and find all four pieces.

explain.text: $(r - m)(r - m)$ has pieces $r^2$, $-mr$, $-mr$ and $+m^2$. So $(r - m)^2 = r^2 - 2mr + m^2$. Averaging this expansion over many returns gives the variance shortcut.

quiz.prose: The first bracket now has $2x$: expand $(2x + 1)(x + 3)$.
quiz.question: Which is it?

options.why: You added 2 and 3 for the middle. The strips are $2x \times 3 = 6x$ and $1 \times x = x$.
You multiplied the firsts and the lasts. The strips $6x$ and $x$ are missing.
You took $2x \times 3$ as $3x$. It is $6x$, plus $x$ from the other strip.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply every term of one bracket by every term of the other.

explain.text: The pieces are $2x \times x = 2x^2$, $2x \times 3 = 6x$, $1 \times x = x$ and $1 \times 3 = 3$. The strips collect to $7x$. So the answer is $2x^2 + 7x + 3$.
